And, to make matters worse, the website makes it virtually impossible to find the manual needed to address replacement of the igniter.  Just going around in circles of advertising and self-kudos.

Results.ReviewText:
I Bought this grill yesterday. It was the only one in this color which I had been looking for. There was no obvious damage to the packaging. Upon getting this grill home and opening the box and unpacking the grill to make sure I had all the pieces I found quite a few upsetting damages. First I was presented with the crack to the handle and a chip in the paint of the lid. I then found the crack to the rear of the lid. Further inspection I found the crack in the grill box. The control console has a crack in it as well. The Weber emblem in the lid is missing a threaded bolt and the nut and washer to hold it on. Finally the warming rack doesn't even fit the slots. 

It appears this grill must have been made and packaged on a Monday. I reached out to customer service to see if I can get these parts replaced and was told it wasn't there problem and I need to contact the dealer (awesome warranty) So now I will be dealing with the dealer and will be without a grill for who know's how long. 

I am no expert but there was no damages to the exterior packaging and the amount of carboard for protection on the inside it appears this happened prior to shipping. Some of the issues the warming tray not even fitting the grill box and the missing emblem pieces are just poor craftmanship. I did not expect this with a Weber grill and just being told to take it back to the dealer is not acceptable. Guess It is back to reading reviews for another grill company.
Results.Title: Terrible Customer Service

Results.ReviewText:
I've bought the cheapest BBQ's I could find for years. They'd last one season, and then next season the grill / burners would be rusted out / degrading, or the sparker wouldn't be working, or the heat distribution would be terrible, having almost cold spots in some area's or extremely hot spots in other areas. The last cheap one I bought shot flames out the back when cooking anything at all.

Finally decided to spend a lot more than I usually would have and buy a Weber. Home Depot had this model on sale so we picked it up. Was it expensive? Yes. Almost a year later, was it worth it? Definitely!

This grill has excellent heat control and heat distribution. The ignition system is reliable. It's sturdy and well built. It burns propane efficiently. Much better than some of the ones I had in the past.

I only have 2 gripes. 1) Where the BBQ base rests on the metal stand it's starting to show signs of rust, even though the BBQ has been under a genuine Weber cover since day 1 and never exposed to rain. 2) All the Weber accessories are really expensive compared to similar products made by someone else. The only accessory that I bought that is genuine Weber was the cover. Everything else was 3rd party.

Results.ReviewText: We've had this grill for about 3 months, and have used it a few times. It works well. However, it's not easy to clean the grate (i.e., the surface on which food is placed). Our last grill (which served us for 20 years) was also from Weber. It had a different grate, which was easier to clean. [Note: Weber recommends a particular brush to clean the grate, and we did purchase and use that brush. The brush DID clean the grate, but it required more time and effort than was necessary to clean the grate on our old grill.] Subject to this issue, we would recommend this grill to others.

Results.ReviewText: I was going to rehab my 2001 Silver B, but the cost for replacement parts and time just didn't seem worth the effort.  Sooo, I went to the big orange store and bought a Spirit II E-310 completely assembled.  First cook last night was some Nebraska sirloins. Perfect!  Granted, the newer grill is not as heavy duty as the older Weber gassers, but with the 10 year warranty I think I will get many years of great grilling.  Only negative is the pesky left side table.  A little hard to move the grill when the table is in the up position, but I'll get the hang of it.  If there was a way to place the left table in a permanent "up" position, that would be great.   Get one...I don't think you'll be disappointed! Very reasonably priced too.
Results.Title: Just amazing!

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: Excellent online consumer-report reviews of this E-310 led to our purchase. Great heat - 2-burners I'd bet is fine if you really need an even smaller grill, but 3 is the way to go to get a little more grate-space and heat. Weber customer service team has been awesome and prompt with any issues concerns I've had - that service alone makes the big-ticket price for this grill well worth the investment.
Results.Title: 3-Burner Grill Is The Right Way to Go

Results.OriginalProductName: Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
Results.ReviewText: I took delivery last Thursday and assembled it last Friday.  It took me 2 1/2 hours to assemble as I did not have any help.  The assembly instructions are a delight, all pictures and no words.  Weber must have taken a leaf out of IKEA's book!  Following all the steps very methodically was very easy.  All the parts were marked on their packing and easy to identify.  So, a pleasure to assemble.  Performancewise, it is fare superior to my old Weber Genesis, which was falling apart as the fasteners holding the lid had corroded.  I was very impressed with the packaging inside the box.  Apart from the plastic bags, which are all recyclable like grocery bags, all of the other packaging was cardboard, which was also recycled.  Years ago it would all have been plastic foam.  So, kudos to Weber for being environmentally aware.
Results.Title: Easy to assemble.  Great grilling performance

Results.ReviewText:
This is my second Weber grill.  My first was the Genesis Series B.  I purchased that grill well over 15 years ago and it was working and looking great when I gave it to my son recently.  So I replaced it with the Spirit II E-310 a couple months ago.  And as far as the grilling is concerned, it's just as good, (if not better) than my Genesis Series B was.  I've also purchased the iGrill 3 (which I've yet to master) and a rotisserie (which is absolutely awesome).  So the cooking part of it is going pretty well.  
However, I am very disappointed in one thing particularly and that is the left hand side table that folds down.  Where I live I don't have the ability to keep my grill in one location permanently, so I have to move it.  But when I go to move it, the metal on the left side table is so flimsy that it bends and comes off every time.  I've tried everything I can think of to keep it from happening, but unfortunately I haven't succeeded.  By the way, this wasn't a problem on my Series B as the left side table wasn't metal and I was able to move it without any problems.  But other than that disappointment, the grill itself doesn't disappoint.  Everything else works great and the end result is always delicious.
Results.Title: Grills Great

Results.ReviewText: This grill is build solid and provides pretty even heat over the whole grilling surface.   Its design allows you to get propane tanks in and out pretty easy and the gauge (based on weight of the tank) to let you know when you need more propane is pretty useful, though not super precise. You pay a little more for a Weber but the build quality is probably worth it, although we have only had ours for 5 months. Time will tell...
